chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Seeing Booker in Brazil shortly before his death
summary: Budd records with Booker in New York, then visits him in Brazil in about 1966-67 when Booker is dying of throat cancer.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And he said that -- he said that he looked good. He looked like his old self. He just had a few grey hairs in his

head, and he said that he felt pretty good. So later on, this must have been about 1966 or 7. Later on I went to South America with Earl HInes and Oscar Peterson, doing some concert tours, and I was in Brazil, and Booker was there in Brazil. And I went by to see him and he was staying with his stepdaughter's grandmamma, and she was taking care of him. He had cancer of the throat, and he said he had tried all kind of treatments. They were really taking care of him good, because now she's a big star, she's making a lot of money, and she's really looking after her stepfather. She loved him.
Well this just was her stepfather. Because I met her real father.
This was her stepfather, Booker was her stepfather, but she looked upon Booker as her real father. She loved him that much. He had done so much for her.

And they had set him up in a beautiful apartment, and given him all the money that he needed to be taken care of, so Booker was saying, 'I've tried all the doctors I can try. Now I'm going to a witch doctor way out in the interior of the country.' And he's giving me -- showed me all of the tonics he was taking, to cure this cancer. Said this guy was noted all over the world for curing cancer.
and come back, And then of course when I left about six months later I learned that he had passed away.
